title: Simplicial model targets detect essentially surjective maps
statement:
Use small simplicial categories, Dwyer--Kan equivalences and the model homotopy category $h\mathrm{sCat}$ from [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property], and combinatorial simplicial model categories from [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. For a simplicial category $T$, write $\pi_0T$ for its category with the same objects and components of mapping simplicial sets as arrows. For a simplicial model category $\mathcal A$, let $\mathcal A^{cf}$ be its full simplicial subcategory of cofibrant fibrant objects. Fix nested universes so that $X,Y$ are small in the smaller universe and the model categories and hom sets used as tests fit in larger universes; permit enlargement to include simplicial presheaves on $X$ and $Y$.

Let $u:X\to Y$ be a morphism in $h\mathrm{sCat}$ such that its induced functor $\pi_0X\to\pi_0Y$, defined up to natural isomorphism, is essentially surjective: every object of $\pi_0Y$ is isomorphic to an image object. Then $u$ is an isomorphism if and only if, for every combinatorial simplicial model category $\mathcal A$, precomposition induces a bijection
$$u^*:\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(Y,\mathcal A^{cf})\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(X,\mathcal A^{cf}).$$
For any actual simplicial functor representing such an isomorphism (allowing cofibrant and fibrant replacements of its endpoints), that functor is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. There is no local Kan or cofibrancy assumption on $X,Y$.

source.place: Lemma A.3.4.6 and Corollary A.3.4.11, printed pp.886 and 889, applied to the target reduction at the start of the proof of Lemma A.3.5.14, printed p.896. This is the essentially-surjective comparison test, not a claim that model targets detect arbitrary non-surjective maps. Read online 2026-10-17; archival HTT WANTED. No Stacks tag states this enriched homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: The forward implication is formal: if $v$ is inverse to $u$, precomposition by $v$ is inverse to precomposition by $u$ for every target. For the converse choose cofibrant-fibrant representatives $X_0,Y_0$ of $X,Y$ in the Bergner model supplied by [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property]. By [lem-coef-model-localization-homotopy-classes], the given morphism has an actual representative $u_0:X_0\to Y_0$. Conjugating by the replacement isomorphisms preserves the test bijections and essential surjectivity. We henceforth write $X,Y,u$ for these representatives. Their mapping sets are Kan: the fibration to the terminal simplicial category has local Kan fibrations by [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. Only replacements, not additional hypotheses on the original categories, have been made.

source.place: Agent expansion of paragraph 2 foundational target reduction; HTT A.3.4.6, initial fibrant replacement, and A.3.5.14, target test

proof.text: For each $T=X,Y$ form $\mathcal P_T=\mathsf{sSet}^{T^{\mathrm{op}}}$ using enriched functors. The Kan-model simplicial-set category is combinatorial and simplicial by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]; hence [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] applies to the small simplicial category $T^{\mathrm{op}}$ and supplies its combinatorial simplicial projective structure. Let $h_t=T(-,t)$. It is cofibrant: it is the free diagram at $t$ on $\Delta^0$, and the free/evaluation adjunction lifts its initial map against every objectwise trivial fibration, since $\varnothing\to\Delta^0$ is a cofibration. It is fibrant because $T(z,t)$ is Kan for every $z$. For cofibrant $P$ and fibrant $Q$, the simplicial model axiom in the calculus node, applied to $\varnothing\to P$ and $Q\to *$, makes $\operatorname{Map}(P,Q)\to *$ a Kan fibration; thus $\mathcal P_T^{cf}$ has Kan mapping sets and is Bergner fibrant by Step 1's criterion. The model target $\mathcal P_T$ is permitted by the universe convention. This invokes the enriched diagram theorem, not the ordinary-index presheaf clause.

source.place: Agent expansion of paragraph 2 supporting target reduction; HTT A.3.4.6 proof, projective enriched presheaves

proof.text: The Yoneda functor $j_T:T\to\mathcal P_T^{cf}$ is strictly fully faithful on mapping simplicial sets. Here is the calculation, including simplicial parameters. A natural map $\alpha:h_t\times\Delta^n\to F$ is sent to the simplex $\alpha_t(1_t,-):\Delta^n\to F(t)$. Conversely, $p:\Delta^n\to F(t)$ gives $(a,s)\mapsto F(a)(p(s))$ at $z$, for $a\in T(z,t)$. Associativity gives enriched naturality, the identity gives evaluation of this inverse equal to $p$, and naturality at $a$ gives the other inverse equation. Both formulas commute with maps $\Delta^m\to\Delta^n$, so they identify the mapping simplicial set with $F(t)$. Taking $F=h_{t'}$ gives $\operatorname{Map}(h_t,h_{t'})\cong T(t,t')$; composition and identities agree by associativity and the unit of $T$. The mapping-set and free-diagram descriptions used here are precisely those of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus].

source.place: Agent explicit enriched Yoneda computation beneath paragraph 2; HTT A.3.4.6 proof, Yoneda embedding

proof.text: Record the needed full-subcategory observation directly in the Bergner model, to avoid the cyclic dependency of the existing general essential-image lemma. Let $S$ be fibrant and $E\subseteq S$ its full subcategory on a collection of objects closed under isomorphism in $\pi_0S$. Then $E$ is fibrant, and $k:E\to S$ is a Bergner fibration: local maps are identities of Kan sets; an invertible vertex out of $e\in E$ has target in $E$ by repleteness, and that same vertex is a lift. The fibration characterization is the $J$-injective criterion of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting] for the model in [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property]. A class $a:Z\to S$ with essential image in $E$ lifts to $E$ in $h\mathrm{sCat}$: represent it by $QZ\to S$ using [lem-coef-model-localization-homotopy-classes]. Its values belong to $E$, since its induced component functor has that essential image. Fullness gives a strict corestriction, with exactly the same maps on mapping sets. This proves the required existence without a coherent-nerve comparison.

source.place: Agent direct Bergner full-subcategory calculation beneath paragraph 2; HTT A.3.4.11(2), replete-full-subcategory special case

proof.text: For the same inclusion $k:E\to S$, postcomposition is injective on $\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(Z,E)$. Replace $Z$ by a cofibrant $QZ$ and represent two classes by $f,g:QZ\to E$. If $kf=kg$ in the homotopy category, [lem-coef-model-localization-homotopy-classes] gives a cylinder $QZ\amalg QZ\xrightarrow{(e_0,e_1)}J\xrightarrow{c}QZ$ with $c$ weak, $ce_i=1$, and $H:J\to S$ with endpoints $kf,kg$. Here $\pi_0c$ is an equivalence because Bergner weak equivalences are DK equivalences. Every object $z$ of $J$ is therefore isomorphic in $\pi_0J$ to $e_0(cz)$: their images under $\pi_0c$ agree and full faithfulness lifts the identity and its inverse. Applying $\pi_0H$ shows $H(z)$ is isomorphic to $f(cz)$, which belongs to $E$. Repleteness forces all values of $H$ into $E$, so fullness corestricts $H$ and supplies the same cylinder homotopy between $f,g$. The reverse implication of the cited node gives $f=g$ in $h\mathrm{sCat}$.

source.place: Agent cylinder proof beneath paragraph 2; HTT A.3.4.11(1), replete-full-subcategory special case

proof.text: Let $E_T\subseteq\mathcal P_T^{cf}$ be the full subcategory on all objects isomorphic in $\pi_0\mathcal P_T^{cf}$ to some $h_t$. It is replete, since composites of isomorphisms are isomorphisms. The functor $j_T$ factors as $T\xrightarrow{e_T}E_T\xrightarrow{k_T}\mathcal P_T^{cf}$. Step 3 makes every mapping map of $e_T$ an isomorphism; its component functor is fully faithful and essentially surjective by definition of $E_T$. Thus $e_T$ is a DK equivalence, hence invertible in the localization [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property]. Steps 4-5 imply that $(j_T)_*$ is injective on maps out of any small $Z$, and that a class $a:Z\to\mathcal P_T^{cf}$ factors through $j_T$ exactly when its component functor has essential image among the representables. Indeed first factor through $k_T$ and then compose with $e_T^{-1}$; injectivity follows by cancelling $k_T$ and $e_T$. All categories fit in the enlarged universe allowed in the statement.

source.place: Agent assembly of Yoneda and the replete-full-subcategory test; HTT A.3.4.6 and A.3.4.11

proof.text: Apply surjectivity of the assumed test for $\mathcal A=\mathcal P_X$ to $[j_X]$. Obtain $F:Y\to\mathcal P_X^{cf}$ in $h\mathrm{sCat}$ with $Fu=j_X$. For any object $y$ of $Y$, essential surjectivity of $\pi_0u$ gives $x$ and an isomorphism $ux\cong y$. Applying $\pi_0F$ and then the natural isomorphism induced by $Fu=j_X$ gives $F(y)\cong j_X(x)$. The interpretation of homotopy classes on $\pi_0$, including independence and natural isomorphism, is supplied by [lem-coef-simplicial-derived-pushout-mapping]. Concretely, since $X,Y$ are cofibrant and $\mathcal P_X^{cf}$ is fibrant, [lem-coef-model-localization-homotopy-classes] represents $F$ and $u$ by actual simplicial functors $F_0,u_0$; then $F_0u_0$ is an actual representative of $Fu=j_X$, its component functor is strictly $\pi_0F_0\circ\pi_0u_0$, and it is naturally isomorphic to $\pi_0j_X$ because the induced functor depends only on the homotopy class. Step 6 now gives $v:Y\to X$ with $j_Xv=F$. Consequently $j_Xvu=Fu=j_X$, and Step 6 injectivity with source $X$ implies $vu=1_X$. This is the only use of essential surjectivity; there is no assumption that $u$ is injective on objects.

source.place: Agent explicit left-inverse construction for paragraph 2 target reduction; HTT A.3.5.14 initial reduction via A.3.4.6 and A.3.4.11

proof.text: Apply injectivity of the assumed test for $\mathcal A=\mathcal P_Y$ to the two maps $j_Yuv,j_Y:Y\to\mathcal P_Y^{cf}$. Their restrictions along $u$ agree, because $j_Yuvu=j_Yu$ by $vu=1_X$. Thus $j_Yuv=j_Y$. Step 6 injectivity, now for $j_Y$ with source $Y$, gives $uv=1_Y$. Therefore $u$ is invertible. For the final assertion, an actual simplicial functor whose class is such an isomorphism is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences], applied to the Bergner model of [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property]. Its weak equivalences are exactly DK equivalences. This applies before or after the allowed endpoint replacements, and supplies the asserted conclusion without endpoint cofibrancy or fibrancy assumptions.

On continuation, explicitly verified that the cofibrant-fibrant test subcategories have Kan mapping sets by the stated simplicial model axiom.

lean.statement: theorem simplicial_model_target_test (X Y : SCat.{max (u + 1) w}) [Small.{u} X] [Small.{u} Y] (_hX : ∀ (x y : X) (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ), Small.{u} ((hom X x y).obj n)) (_hY : ∀ (x y : Y) (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ), Small.{u} ((hom Y x y).obj n)) (f : bergnerHomotopyFunctor.obj X ⟶ bergnerHomotopyFunctor.obj Y) (_hf : IsEssentiallySurjective f) : (IsIso f ↔ ∀ (C : Type (max (u + 1) w)) [Category.{u} C] [ModelCategory C] [SimplicialCategory C] (_T : SimplicialTensorCotensor C), CombinatorialModelCategory.{max (u + 1) w, u, u} C → SimplicialModelLocalization.SatisfiesSM7 C → Function.Bijective (fun a : bergnerHomotopyFunctor.obj Y ⟶ bergnerHomotopyFunctor.obj (liftBundle (BifibrantObject C)) ↦ f ≫ a)) ∧ (IsIso f → ∀ (A B : SCat.{max (u + 1) w}) (g : A ⟶ B) (eX : bergnerHomotopyFunctor.obj A ≅ bergnerHomotopyFunctor.obj X) (eY : bergnerHomotopyFunctor.obj B ≅ bergnerHomotopyFunctor.obj Y), bergnerHomotopyFunctor.map g ≫ eY.hom = eX.hom ≫ f → DwyerKanEquivalence (A := underlying A) (B := underlying B) g)
lean.note: The ambient Bergner homotopy category is in max (u+1) w, with Small.{u} source objects and mapping degrees. Model tests are locally u-small with objects in that larger universe, including enriched simplicial presheaf models. Uses the existing degreewise liftBundle on the actual full bifibrant subcategory; essential surjectivity is tested on a three-arrow representative, with no endpoint fibrancy or cofibrancy assumption.
